Likhita
------------------------------------------
The dharmasūtra work of शङ्ख-लिखित is considered as very authoritative by the Vājasaneyins (followers of Śukla Yajurveda).
As per the story in the Mahābhārata (Śāntiparva 23.18-43) लिखित once went to the hermitage of his elder brother शङ्ख. Since शङ्ख had gone out, लिखित had to wait until he returned. During this time he saw some nice fruits hanging from the trees in the garden, plucked a few and ate them. When शङ्ख returned and found what लिखित had done, he admonished him for this act of his, as theft and advised him to go to the king Sudyumna to receive appropriate punishment.
Though Sudyumna refused to give punishment—since लिखित was well-known as a sage of great rectitude—he was obliged to do so due to लिखित’s insistence. As per the law, both the hands of लिखित were cut off. When he arrived at शङ्ख’s hermitage again and reported to him of having received the punishment, शङ्ख advised him to take bath in the nearby river. As soon as लिखित did so, he got back both his hands, due to the mysterious power exercised by शङ्ख.
Likhita was the co-author of the धर्मसूत्रस्, along with his brother शङ्ख.
